full_text:
A notoriously stingy landlord named Kuberappa was embarrassed by his reputation as a miser. To improve his social standing, he invited all the scholars, poets, and councilors of Vijayanagara, including Tenali Raman, to an 'Imperial Eight-Course Banquet' at his grand mansion.

The guests arrived, their mouths watering in anticipation.
They were seated upon silk cushions around an empty dining hall.
Kuberappa entered, clapped his hands with theatrical enthusiasm, and said:
'Welcome, noble guests! Let the feast begin!
Imagine, my friends! Look at the imaginary silver platters before you!
Behold this celestial saffron rice cooked in pure ghee! Inhale its divine aroma!
Taste these imaginary almond laddus, crisp samosas, and roasted partridges!
Eat, my friends, eat of the feast of imagination!'

The bewildered guests sat in stunned silence with empty plates.
While the other scholars frowned in angry disgust, Tenali Raman smiled with supreme enthusiasm!
Tenali pretended to scoop up imaginary rice with his fingers, smacking his lips with loud relish:
'Ah! Divine! Magnificent! Kuberappa, your imaginary samosas are crispy, and your imaginary payasam is sweeter than nectar!'
Tenali chewed the empty air, swallowed imaginary sweets, and rubbed his stomach with theatrical joy:
'I have never eaten so well in all my life!'

Kuberappa was delighted, thinking Tenali was supporting his cheap trick.

As the gathering concluded, Kuberappa accompanied the guests to the front gate.
Tenali Raman turned to Kuberappa, bowed low, and reached into his pocket.
Tenali pulled out an empty fist, held it over Kuberappa’s open palm, and pantomimed dropping fifty heavy gold coins into the landlord's hand:
'Here, noble Kuberappa! Take this generous tip of fifty imaginary gold coins for your magnificent feast!
Feel their heavy, glittering weight! Buy yourself fifty imaginary cows and an imaginary palace of marble!'

Kuberappa stared at his completely empty hand:
'Tenali! My hand is empty! You have given me nothing!'

Tenali laughed with booming joy:
'Why, noble host! If an imaginary saffron banquet can fill the bellies of twenty hungry scholars, surely fifty imaginary gold coins will fill your treasury to overflowing!
You fed us on empty air, and I have paid you with phantom gold!
The account is balanced to the last coin!'

The entire gathering burst into roaring laughter, while Kuberappa turned red as a beet.
Humiliated by the lesson, Kuberappa rushed to his kitchen, ordered his cooks to light the fires, and served the guests an actual, lavish feast of real rice, ghee, and sweets, learning that hospitality must be real to earn real honor.
moral: Miserly hosts who promise grand banquets but serve empty airs deserve to feast on imaginary fragrances. [ES]
